name: Gildhaven
subtitle: Market Day on the River Gild
author: Luminati
description: A 128 × 128 walled river town on fair day: High Town and Sunspire Abbey on the terrace, the Gildfall, the Market Square on the river, the West and East Quarters, the Gild Pool harbour, the rows of Lantern Row and Weaver's Lane, and Fairfield outside the South Gate with the players' stage and the mill. Generated by tools/make-gildhaven.mjs.

title.title: GILDHAVEN
title.subtitle: Market Day on the River Gild

objects.name: Sunspire Abbey
text: The great door stands ajar. Inside, a hundred candles and one very patient choir.
A brass plate by the door: "{The Sunspire Bell} rings the fair closed at dusk. Kindly do not ring it yourself. — The Abbess"
The {Sun Well}. Its water is said to taste of honey on fair day.
It tastes of water. Very good water, to be fair.

objects.name: Gildhaven Hall
text: A footman opens the door an inch: "The Lord Mayor is receiving in the court today, as it is fair day. And as it is sunny."

objects.name: Thornbury House
text: A maid peers out. "Lady Thornbury is not at home. Lady Thornbury is at the fair, buying a hat she does not need."

objects.name: The Guild Exchange
text: Through the door: the clatter of an abacus and somebody saying "Twelve barrels? I said TWO barrels!"

objects.name: Larkspur House
text: Nobody answers, but a parrot inside says "Fair day! Fair day!" with great conviction.

objects.name: The Gilt Library
text: A card in the window: "SILENCE. (This means you, the fair.)"

objects.name: Quillon House
text: The brass knocker is shaped like a quill. Knocking with it leaves a small ink stain on your knuckles.

objects.name: The Watch House
text: A duty roster is nailed to the door. Somebody has written "FAIR DAY — EVERYONE" across all of it.

objects.name: Almsfield House
text: A cheerful voice: "Come back after the bell! We are all down at the fair until then — even the kettle."

objects.speaker: Signpost
text:
↘ {The Lookout} over the {Gild Pool}
↙ the {Harbour Stair} down to the {North Quay}

objects.name: Pippin Cottage
text: Apple-crates are stacked high by the door. A note: "Gone to sell apples. Take one, leave a coin. — H."

objects.speaker: Signpost
text:
{Pippin Orchard}
Apples for the fair: take one, leave a coin.

objects.name: The Salt Store
text: Locked. Through a crack: sacks of salt piled to the rafters, and a cat asleep on the highest one.

objects.name: The Customs House
text: A sign: "ALL BARGES TO DECLARE ALL CARGO. Including cheese. ESPECIALLY cheese."

objects.name: Tamsin's Boatyard
text: The smell of pitch and sawdust. Somebody inside is singing to a boat. The boat does not seem to mind.

objects.name: The Harbour Office
text: "Back in five minutes," says the note. It has said so since this morning.

objects.speaker: Signpost
text:
↑ the {Grand Stair} · {Sunspire Abbey}
← the {Gildfall} · → the {Harbour Stair}
The {Gild Well}. They say the first barge-folk washed gold dust out of the river here, and the town was named for it.
The water glints. Probably the sun. Probably.

objects.speaker: Signpost

objects.name: The Gilded Goose
text: Laughter, a fiddle and the smell of roast apples spill out of {The Gilded Goose}.
Above the door hangs a goose of beaten gold leaf. It has been stolen eleven times. It always comes back.

objects.name: The Ropewalk
text: A long shed full of hemp and twisting rope. "Mind your fingers," calls a voice, "or you become rope."

objects.name: Cliffside Cottage
text: A cosy voice: "We can hear the Gildfall from our beds. We have not had a dry pillow since the spring."

objects.name: Gildfall Mill
text: Flour dust puffs out under the door. The millstones rumble like a giant clearing its throat.

objects.speaker: Signpost
text:
→ the {Mistbridge} to the {North Quay}
↓ {Mill Lane} to {Market Street}

objects.name: Joss Plane's Carpentry
text: Sawdust drifts from the door. A half-finished rocking horse stares at you with one painted eye.

objects.name: The Tannery
text: A smell hits you before the door does. You decide not to knock twice.

objects.name: The Barrelhouse
text: Barrels rumble somewhere inside. A cheerful bellow: "We are OPEN, it is FAIR DAY, and the ale is BROWN!"

objects.name: The Dye Works
text: Blue, gold and red cloth hangs drying inside. The dyer's hands are, you suspect, all three colours.

objects.name: Hammerstane Smithy
text: The ring of a hammer stops. "If you want a horseshoe, wait. If you want a sword, wait longer. If you want to chat, Rurik is outside."

objects.name: Odd & Sons, Chandlers
text: Rope, tar, candles, nails, a stuffed pike and, for some reason, a harp. "We have everything," says the sign. It may be right.

objects.name: The Saltcellar
text: A bargeman's home. Somebody inside is snoring in time with the river.

objects.name: The Boathouse
text: Upturned boats inside, and a dozen oars, and a gull that very clearly lives here now.

objects.speaker: Signpost
text:
→ the {Fish Quay} · the {Piers} · the {Boathouse}
← the {Market Square}

objects.name: The Wheelwright's
text: A wheel leans by the door, waiting for its cart. It looks like it has been waiting a while.

objects.name: Pegg's Cobblery
text: A sign in the window: "Shoes mended. Boots mended. Hearts not mended, try the Abbey."

objects.name: The Potter's House
text: A wheel hums inside. A pot slumps. Somebody sighs, then laughs, then starts again.

objects.name: Rosehip Cottage
text: Roses climb all the way to the chimney. A voice: "If you have come about the roses, they are not for sale. They are for showing off."

objects.name: The Saffron Bakery
text: The door is warm. Behind it: saffron, butter and a very busy oven.

objects.name: The Apothecary
text: Bottles of every colour line the window. One of them is gently bubbling. You decide not to ask.

objects.name: Needle & Thimble
text: A dummy in the window wears half a very fine coat. The other half is presumably on its way.

objects.name: The Scrivener's
text: "Letters written, read, and — for a small extra fee — improved."

objects.name: Tick & Tock, Clockmakers
text: Dozens of clocks tick inside, none of them together. It is, apparently, every time at once.

objects.name: The Toymaker's
text: A wooden soldier in the window salutes as the door creaks. Clever springs.

objects.name: The Cooperage
text: Hoops and staves everywhere. A half-made barrel rocks gently, like it is thinking about rolling off.

objects.name: Wick's Lantern Shop
text: Lanterns of every size hang in the window, waiting for dusk like children waiting for a story.

objects.name: The Net Loft
text: Nets drying in great brown waves. It smells of the sea, and slightly of someone's lunch.

objects.name: Gullscry Cottage
text: A very small cottage with a very large door knocker, as if to make up for it.

objects.name: Brine House
text: The harbourmaster's house. A brass telescope pokes out of the upstairs window, though there is no upstairs.

objects.name: The Weaver's House
text: The clack of a loom. A voice counts "...forty-one, forty-two, forty — oh, BOTHER."

objects.name: Hollyhock House
text: Hollyhocks by the door, taller than you. They nod as if they know you.

objects.name: Widow Fenn's
text: "Come in if you are a grandchild, go away if you are selling something, and wipe your feet either way."

objects.name: The Gate Watch
text: Empty. A kettle on the hob and two mugs, both labelled "SERGEANT".

objects.name: Candlewick Cottage
text: The whole house smells of beeswax. Even the doorknob is slightly sticky.

objects.name: Hearthstone House
text: A big family by the sound of it, all of them looking for the same left shoe.

objects.name: The Dame School
text: Closed for the fair. A slate by the door reads: "NO SCHOOL TODAY. Yes, really. Go away. — Dame Agnes"

objects.name: Sorrel's Herbs
text: Bundles of drying herbs hang so thick inside that the room looks like a little forest.

objects.name: The Bathhouse
text: Warm steam curls out under the door. "Baths half price on fair day," says the slate. "Soap extra. Singing free."

objects.name: Shrine of the Tide
text: Shells and smooth stones line the doorstep: offerings for boats that come home, and for some that did not.

objects.speaker: Signpost
text:
{Bellgreen}
Please do not climb the oak. (It means you, Kit.)

objects.name: Quern Cottage
text: Flour on the doorstep, flour on the knocker, flour on you now.

objects.name: Barlow's Farmhouse
text: "BARLOW'S EGGS — the best in Fairfield" is painted over the door. Underneath, smaller: "the only in Fairfield".

objects.name: Sergeant Brask
dialogue: Welcome to {Gildhaven}, traveller. Gild Fair today, so the gate stands open and my patience stands closed.
Market Square is straight up {Main Street}. Fair stalls, the players and the mill are out here in {Fairfield}.

objects.name: Corporal Lisbet
dialogue: The sergeant counts everyone who comes in. I count everyone who goes out. We have never once agreed.
If you see a little boy with a toffee apple and no shoes, that is {Nim}. He is fine. He is always fine.

objects.name: Florin Fiddlewick
dialogue: Ah, an audience! The {Wandering Lark Players}, at your service — songs, dances, and one juggler who is mostly reliable.
We play the Gild Fair every year. The town pays us in pies, and the pies are worth the walk.

objects.name: Mirela
dialogue: Clap on the off-beat, if you please. Florin is always half a beat ahead, and somebody has to drag him back.
After the fair we follow the {King's Road} south. Next week, a wedding. Then a funeral. Then another wedding. Busy season.

objects.name: Corwin the Juggler
dialogue: Three apples, two knives and a turnip. The turnip is the dangerous one. Nobody expects the turnip.

objects.name: Hetty Bramble
dialogue: Toffee apples! Dipped this morning, sticky till midnight.
The apples come from {Pippin Orchard} up in {High Town}. The toffee comes from me. The teeth are your own business.

objects.name: Rosalind
dialogue: Fair ribbons! Tie one on your wrist and the music finds you. That is the custom. Or I made it up. One of those.

objects.name: Edda
dialogue: I walked in from the farms at dawn for this. My feet hurt and I would not be anywhere else.

objects.name: Old Ambrose
dialogue: Sixty-one Gild Fairs I have seen. The players get younger every year. The juggler never gets better.

objects.name: Daro the Wayfarer
dialogue: Came up the {King's Road} from the coast. You can smell the fair from a mile off — toffee, woodsmoke and cattle.
Mind you, the town is the real sight. The Abbey up on the rock, the falls coming off the cliff... worth the blisters.

objects.name: Farmer Barlow
dialogue: Barlow's the name, eggs are the game. Brown eggs, white eggs, and one blue egg nobody can explain.
If you catch my boy {Nim} chasing the hens again, tell him supper is when the {Sunspire Bell} rings.

objects.name: Nim
dialogue: I am not CHASING them. I am HERDING them. There is a difference and the difference is I am winning.

objects.name: Tobias Quern
dialogue: Fairfield Mill grinds for half the valley. On fair day, it grinds for the bakers, and the bakers grind me.
Down in town there's an older mill, under the {Gildfall}. Runs on water, not wind. Show-off.

objects.name: Crier Bertil
dialogue: HEAR YE, HEAR YE! The Gild Fair is OPEN! Stalls on the square, players in {Fairfield}, and fish on the {Fish Quay}!
At dusk the {Sunspire Bell} rings the fair closed, and the Lord Mayor lights the lanterns along the river. Bring a coat. And a sweetheart, if you have one going spare.
Lady {Odelia Fairgild}. She receives in the court of {Gildhaven Hall} on fair day — up the {Grand Stair} and west along {Crown Walk}, over the Hall Bridge.

objects.name: Dora Haddock
dialogue: Fresh this morning! Gild trout, river eels, and a pike so ugly it frightened the cat.

objects.name: Azar
dialogue: Saffron, pepper, cinnamon bark — all the way up the river by barge, all the way from the sea.
One pinch of my saffron and the bakers of {Lantern Row} fight in the street. I have seen it. I sold them tickets.

objects.name: Pim Crumble
dialogue: Bread! Bread! Bread with seeds, bread without seeds, bread shaped like a goose for the fair.

objects.name: Signora Vell
dialogue: River-blue cloth, dyed in the {West Quarter} and fit for a duchess. Feel it. No — gently. GENTLY.

objects.name: Ottilie Clay
dialogue: Cups, jugs, and a teapot that pours almost entirely into the cup. Almost.

objects.name: Goodman Hollis
dialogue: Eggs from Barlow's Farm, hens from my own yard. Those four by the stall are not for sale. They are staff.

objects.name: Daisy
dialogue: Marigolds for the fair! You wear them to the bell at dusk, then throw them in the river for luck.

objects.name: Master Brie
dialogue: Cheese. Hard cheese, soft cheese, cheese that walks to you if you leave it long enough. Taste? It is free. The second taste is not.

objects.name: Mother Wenna
dialogue: Welcome to {The Gilded Goose}! Every room is full of fair-folk, but I always keep one bed aired for a traveller.
The goose over the door? Real gold leaf. It gets stolen every year and it always comes back. I suspect it enjoys the trip.

dialogue.text: Tired already? Rest now and you'll miss the bell at dusk.

objects.name: Garr the Bargeman
dialogue: Three days up the river from the sea, and every lock-keeper wanted a fair-day tip. My barge has gone back down without me. I stayed for the cheese.
You should see the {Gild Pool} past the {Barge Quay} — gulls stealing everything that is not nailed down, and some things that are.

objects.name: Sister Wynn
dialogue: Bless you. I came down from {Sunspire Abbey} for cheese and came away with cheese, a ribbon and a goose loaf.
Mother Celandine will ring the bell at dusk. Listen from the {Rampart Walk} — the whole town hums with it.

objects.name: Tilda
dialogue: I have a list. Cheese, cloth, eggs, saffron. I have bought three ribbons. The list is not going well.

objects.name: Beck
dialogue: Sold my furs by noon. Now I am just here for the crowd. And the bread. Mostly the bread.

objects.name: Tilly
dialogue: I am counting pigeons. There are six. There were seven. I think one went to {High Town} to be fancy.
Do you know {Kit}? Kit climbs the oak on {Bellgreen} even though there is a sign. There is a sign because of Kit.

objects.name: Wren
dialogue: Goodman Hollis says the hens are STAFF. So I am helping them do their job. Their job is running.

objects.name: Corporal Dunn
dialogue: Keep your purse close today. Fair days bring three things to {Gildhaven}: farmers, players and fingers.
If you lose something, the {Watch House} is up in {High Town}, east along {Crown Walk}. Captain Hale will be up at the {Lookout}, mind — she always is.

objects.name: Fennick
dialogue: Me? Just browsing. Admiring. Absolutely not counting anyone's purse.
Lovely day. Lovely crowd. Lovely... heavy... cloth.

objects.name: Old Salt Merrow
dialogue: Forty years I have fished the Gild. On fair day the trout hide under the barges, sulking at the noise.
Mind the Grand Stair behind me — three hundred years of feet have made it slippy as a wet eel.

objects.name: Master Odd
dialogue: Customs. Every barge declares its cargo, and I write it in the book. Today I have written "cheese" one hundred and four times.
The {Saltbridge} to the east, {Kingsbridge} in the middle, and the {Mistbridge} by the falls — three bridges, and I have to count the tolls on all of them.

objects.name: Tamsin
dialogue: I build boats. Little ones for the river, bigger ones for the harbour. The biggest one is still a dream and some sawdust.

objects.name: Alba Quern
dialogue: My cousin runs the windmill out in {Fairfield}. I run the water mill under the {Gildfall}. We do not speak of whose flour is better. Mine is.
Stand on the {Mistbridge} when the sun is low — the spray glitters like the gold dust of the old stories. Free of charge, which is more than my cousin can say.

objects.name: Rurik Hammerstane
dialogue: Stand back from the forge, friend. Sparks do not care whose coat they land on.
Fair day means horseshoes, cart-pins and cauldron handles. Nobody buys a sword on fair day. Too much joy in the air.

objects.name: Hamish Mott
dialogue: The {Barrelhouse}! Gild Ale, brown as the river and twice as strong. We brew it with water from the falls.

objects.name: Joss Plane
dialogue: Carpenter. I made half the stalls on the square, and all the benches. If one wobbles, it was the other half.

objects.name: Harbourmaster Ysolde
dialogue: The {Gild Pool}. The barges came up at dawn, unloaded for the fair and went straight back down to the sea for more. Now it is just us and the gulls.
East Pier for fishing, West Pier for gossip. Gran Tessaly mends nets down on the beach, past the smokehouse.

objects.name: Dob
dialogue: Shh. They are biting. Or they were, until you walked down the pier like a drum.

objects.name: Merrit
dialogue: Gulls took my lunch, my bait and my hat. I am keeping the rod out of spite.

objects.name: Gran Tessaly
dialogue: Mending nets, dear. Every hole is a fish that got away and a story that got bigger.
Look up at the cliff. That is the {Lookout}, at the end of the {Rampart Walk}. Captain Hale watches the barges from there, and pretends she is not watching me.

objects.name: Fenna
dialogue: Smoked Gild trout, fresh off the fire at the end of the quay. Smoked eel for the brave.

objects.name: Old Wick
dialogue: Lamplighter. Every lamp from the {South Gate} to the {Rampart Walk} — I light them all at dusk, one by one.
Takes me till the bell has stopped ringing. By then the first ones want trimming. A lamplighter's work is never done, only dim.

objects.name: Bramwell Bun
dialogue: Saffron buns, hot from the {Saffron Bakery}! The saffron comes from Azar's stall on the square. Azar charges like a pirate, but oh, the colour.

objects.name: Saffi
dialogue: I weave the river-blue that Signora Vell sells on the square. She sells it for three times what she pays me. I weave slower on Mondays.

objects.name: Hob
dialogue: Sit down, sit down. The best view of fair day is a bench and a friend.

objects.name: Hester
dialogue: Hob has been on that bench since the fair opened. I have been on this one. We are having a lovely day together.

objects.name: Kit
dialogue: The sign says don't climb the oak. It does not say don't climb the oak AGAIN.

objects.name: Dame Agnes
dialogue: No school today. I said so on the slate. Twice. And on the door. And to every child personally.
They still came. They are at the fair now, learning arithmetic from the cheese stall.

objects.name: Brother Tuck
dialogue: The {Shrine of the Tide} keeps the names of the boats. Those that came home, and those that did not.
Light a thought for the river, friend. It gives this town everything — even its name.

objects.name: Ned the Porter
dialogue: Mind your backs! Barrels for the {Barrelhouse}, cheese for the square, and a harp for — honestly, I do not know who orders a harp.
The chandlers on {Market Street}, probably. They have everything.

objects.name: Ada
dialogue: Have you seen a small boy in a red cap? Answers to "Bram", and to "cake", and to nothing else.

objects.name: Bram
dialogue: Shh! I am hiding from Mum. If she says "cake", I have to come out. It is the rules.

objects.name: Milla
dialogue: Milk! Fresh this morning from {Fairfield}! ...Sold out by noon. I am just walking the empty pails home, for the exercise.

objects.name: Tam the Piper
dialogue: A tune for a penny! A sad one for two! A sad one about pennies for three!
The players out in {Fairfield} have a fiddle. I have a pipe and a good loud hat. We are not rivals. They are simply wrong.

objects.name: Gwen the Bargewife
dialogue: My barge went back down to the sea at noon. Left me here with a pocketful of coin and no boat. I call that a holiday.

objects.name: Lady Odelia Fairgild
dialogue: Welcome to {Gildhaven}, traveller, on the best day of our year. I am Odelia Fairgild, Lord Mayor — "Lord" because the charter is very old and nobody likes paperwork.
Long ago the barge-folk found gold dust in the river below the falls. There was not much, but they named the town for it, and they have been gilding everything since.

dialogue.text: Will you stay for the bell at dusk?

dialogue: Mother {Celandine} rings the {Sunspire Bell}, the fair closes, and we light lanterns all along the river. The water turns to gold for a night. That is the real gild of {Gildhaven}.

objects.name: Guardsman Pell
dialogue: Gildhaven Hall. The Lord Mayor is receiving in the court — just there, by the benches. Please do not curtsey into the flower boxes.

objects.name: Mother Celandine
dialogue: Peace on your fair day. I am the Abbess of {Sunspire Abbey}. At dusk I ring the bell, and the whole town stops to listen.
Three hundred years that bell has rung. It cracked once, in a hard winter. We mended it with gold leaf — a little of everything in Gildhaven is.

objects.name: Novice Cass
dialogue: I polish the candlesticks, I sweep the steps, and at dusk I am allowed to hold the rope while Mother Celandine rings the bell. It is the best job in {Gildhaven}.

objects.name: Elric the Pilgrim
dialogue: I walked from the coast to hear the {Sunspire Bell}. Three weeks. My boots are holier than I am.

objects.name: Brother Anselm
dialogue: The {Gilt Library}: four thousand books, three readers, and one cat who sleeps on the rarest of them.
If you want the history of the fair, it is in chapter nine. If you want the gossip, it is in the Barrelhouse.

objects.name: Guildmaster Orrin
dialogue: The Guild Exchange sets the price of everything sold on the square today. Everything. Even the turnip the juggler drops.
Trade is the river that runs under the river, friend. And this is a very good day for it.

objects.name: Captain Hale
dialogue: The {Lookout}. From here I can see both piers of the {Gild Pool}, every roof in the lower town and the road all the way to the gate.
Quiet fair so far. One stolen purse, one lost child — found asleep in a haystack in {Fairfield} — and the goose went missing from the inn again. It will turn up.

objects.name: Sorrel
dialogue: I keep the Rampart lawns and the Abbey beds. Every fair, somebody sits on my marigolds. Every fair, I forgive them. Barely.

objects.name: Lady Amabel Thornbury
dialogue: I have bought a hat. I did not need a hat. It is the most beautiful hat in {Gildhaven}, and therefore the world.

objects.name: Hazel
dialogue: Pippin Orchard. Every apple on every toffee stick at the fair grew on these trees.
You came over the {Hall Bridge}? Then you have crossed the Gild twice today — once up here as a stream, once down there as a river.
